You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer driver-profile):
- file: driver/cmd_profile.cpp:248
- category: bug-report
- title: profile silently ignores run-only flags --runtime and --step-timeout-ms, contradicting its own reject-loudly policy
- detail: cmd_profile.cpp:241-263 declares 'reject run-only flags loudly instead of silently ignoring them' and rejects --mode/--trigger/--pc-start/--pc-end/--verify/--kanata/--gdb/--gdb-port/--print-memmap. But cli.cpp:111 and :116 parse --runtime and --step-timeout-ms for every subcommand, and grep shows both are consumed only by cmd_run.cpp (lines 186-804 for cli.runtime, 613 for cli.step_timeout_ms) - cmd_profile never reads them and never rejects them. So 'andesim profile --runtime linux app.elf' silently profiles the bare-metal app WITHOUT the vlinux proxy kernel (a different workload than the hybrid run the report's measure: windows target), and --step-timeout-ms is silently dropped. tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh section 2g ('run-only flags are rejected loudly, not silently ignored') tests only --trigger/--mode/--verify, so the gap is untested.
- claimed safety: This is a behavior gap, not a structural refactor - flagged for separate handling per instructions. The fix (two more rows in the runonly[] array at cmd_profile.cpp:247-257) only turns a silent ignore into exit 2 with the existing 'not a profile option' message; no passing use case changes because the flags currently do nothing under profile.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.
